model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on tangible book (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E net revenue, defined as net interest income less retailer share arrangements (RSA) plus other income -- the line SYF's own efficiency ratio uses. H1-2026 actual 7,416 (NII 9,243 - RSA 2,097 + other income 270; H1-2025 7,365) plus H2-2025's 7,616 grown 3% for the fall-2026 Walmart/OnePay launch and NIM build off the Q2 trough. FY2025 actual 14,981 (NII 18,466 - RSA 4,005 + 520); FY2024 16,125 incl. the 1,069 Pets Best gain (15,056 ex-gain). Provision for credit losses is a cost inside the margin, not a revenue deduction.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 10-Q cover-page common shares 325,370,840 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding as of 2026-07-17) plus 2.8M dilutive awards (Q2-2026 WeightedAverageNumberDilutedSharesOutstandingAdjustment). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside other expense and buybacks ($900M Q1, $878M Q2 2026) are the FCFE distribution mechanism, not a modelled count reduction. Q3-2026 repurchases (~$850-900M guided pace) not yet reported; the Q3 10-Q (due ~21 Oct) will reduce the count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank convention (house precedent NAB.AX, HBAN, NTRS, STT): deposits ($82.8B) and securitized/senior/sub debt (CSV total_debt 16,432 at 2026-06-30) are the operating funding of a deposit-taker, already serviced inside net interest income. FCFE is post-interest, so net debt is held at 0 and flows are capitalised at the cost of equity. Cash (16,193) is regulatory liquidity, not surplus. Only the preferred stock (senior to common) is deducted, in equity_bridge.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: net income ~3,200 (guided diluted EPS $9.25-9.50 x ~330M average diluted shares = 3,094 to common + ~100 preferred dividends; pretax ~4,240 = 27.8% margin at 24.5% tax) less ~230 capital retention at 0.8 x FY26's 1.9% net-revenue growth on ~0.9x revenue of TCE. reported_fcf is FY2025 operating cash flow (9,851, no capex tag) -- for a lender this is dominated by the provision add-back and is not free cash flow; recorded for auditability only. The owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: ESTIMATED: SYF does not disclose stock-based compensation expense on the cash-flow statement or in XBRL (no ShareBasedCompensation tag); it sits inside Employee costs (FY2025 2,093). The Statement of Equity 'Stock-based compensation' line is net of withholding (FY2025 74, FY2024 159 incl. 137 treasury reissue). 135 (~0.9% of net revenue) is an estimate; because SBC is already inside other expense the pretax margin is post-SBC, so the estimate only affects the street (SBC-as-non-cash) band, not the house value.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income is the business for a lender. No cash is added back, so there is no double count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock 2,941 + common dividends 427 = 3,368 vs 3,469 net income to common (97% payout). H1-2026 buybacks 1,778 + dividends 204. $6.5B authorization from Q2-2026; quarterly dividend raised to $0.34 from Q3-2026.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the FY2026 guided estimate (year closes 31 Dec 2026, nine months elapsed); Y1 = FY2027. Last full reported year FY2025. Q4-2026 earnings are not in the flows (same convention as NTRS) -- a small conservatism of ~$2.5/share.

balance_sheet_anchors.intangibles_note: Q2-2026 10-Q recast internal-use software out of 'Intangible assets, net' (12/31/25 restated 1,255 -> 104), so TCE is higher than on the FY2025 10-K basis.
balance_sheet_anchors.excess_capital_note: ~1.8B of CET1 above an ~11.5% operating level is NOT added to the bridge: it is treated as the capital that funds the Walmart/OnePay receivables ramp, which is why FY2027 retention is set at 0.5x rather than 0.8x revenue growth.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 12.0% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.55 (SYF's market beta runs 1.4-1.7; near-prime card book is more credit-cyclical than a diversified bank, cf. 9.75% used for the custody bank NTRS). Single rate across scenarios so risk is charged once, through the probability weights and the bear's recession path. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine field; no debt is in the capital structure being discounted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial for a card issuer; rent is inside other expense, no lease line modelled.
inputs.nci_treatment: None; Synchrony Bank is wholly owned.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (house precedent NAB.AX, IAG.AX, GL, HBAN, NTRS, STT) rather than the routing table's residual-income-on-TBV, per the task brief and so SYF is comparable to the other US banks. Mapping onto engine fields: revenue = net revenue (NII - RSA + other income); EBITDA - SBC - D&A = pretax income after provision (provision for credit losses is the dominant cost and lives inside the margin); capex - D&A = equity retained to keep CET1 at target as the book grows (~0.8 x revenue growth as % of revenue, TCE being ~0.9x net revenue); cash tax 24.5% (H1-2026 ETR 24.3%, Q2 25.4%). net_debt 0; preferred deducted in equity_bridge. Pretax margin history on this revenue definition: FY16 32.5%, FY17 26.9%, FY18 27.4%, FY19 36.7%, FY20 16.1%, FY21 54.0% (reserve release), FY22 33.9%, FY23 21.3%, FY24 23.1% ex-gain, FY25 30.8%, H1-26 30.1%; FY26E guidance-implied 27.8% (H2 reserve build for new programs).

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock (Series A, B and 2026 issue) at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: 10-Q 2026-06-30 PreferredStockValue; $494M new preferred issued H1-2026. Preferred dividends (~$100M/yr) are therefore not also deducted from the flows.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 32.7% and NI 5yr 20.7% diverge >30% from equity 5.7%: FY2020 is a COVID provisioning trough (EPS 2.28), and per-share growth is buyback-driven (diluted shares 590.8M FY2020 -> 334.1M Q2-2026, -43%). Total equity barely grows because SYF distributes ~100% of earnings.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue = NII - RSA + other income (FY2016 10,972; FY2020 11,162; FY2022 11,674; FY2025 14,981; FY2024 ex Pets Best gain). FCF CAGRs not meaningful for a lender (OCF is provision-dominated); NI is the FCFE base. No SBC distortion: SBC is small (~0.9% of revenue) and already expensed.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin (EBITDA - SBC - D&A) = [27.5, 28.5, 29.0, 28.5, 28.0, 28, 28, 28, 28, 28]% of net revenue
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = capital retention = [3.0, 4.4, 4.0, 3.6, 3.2, 3.2, 2.8, 2.8, 2.4, 2.4]% of net revenue (~0.8 x revenue growth; zero when the book shrinks)
base.narrative: Walmart/OnePay and Amazon BNPL lift receivables growth to ~6% in FY27 then fade to 3%; pretax margin settles at a 28% through-cycle level (FY2016-25 average 30.3% incl. the 2021 reserve-release freak, 27.8% ex-2021), i.e. one mild credit downturn is priced inside the base.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin (EBITDA - SBC - D&A) = [29.0, 30.5, 31.0, 31.0, 30.5, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30]% of net revenue
bull.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = capital retention = [4.0, 6.4, 5.6, 4.8, 4.4, 4.0, 3.6, 3.2, 2.8, 2.8]% of net revenue (~0.8 x revenue growth; zero when the book shrinks)
bull.narrative: Walmart/OnePay becomes a top-5 program and NIM rebuilds above 15% as late-fee headwinds roll off; net charge-offs stay below the 5.5-6.0% target and pretax margin holds ~30% (FY2019/FY2022/FY2025 level).

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin (EBITDA - SBC - D&A) = [21.0, 15.0, 22.0, 25.0, 26.5, 26.5, 26.5, 26.5, 26.5, 26.5]% of net revenue
bear.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = capital retention = [1.6, 0.0, 0.8, 2.4, 2.4, 2.4, 2.4, 2.4, 2.0, 2.0]% of net revenue (~0.8 x revenue growth; zero when the book shrinks)
bear.narrative: US consumer recession in FY27-28: charge-offs to ~8%, reserve build, receivables shrink 3%; pretax margin troughs at 15% (FY2020 was 16.1%) and recovers only to 26.5% as CFPB/state fee rules and partner RSA renegotiations cap economics.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default: a near-prime card book is among the most credit-cycle-sensitive equities in the folder (FY2020 pretax margin halved), partner concentration (Walmart was lost once in 2019) and CFPB/state fee rulemaking are live, and charge-offs at 4.9% (Aug-26) are below the 5.5-6.0% through-cycle target, i.e. credit is nearer a good point than a bad one. Same weighting as the NTRS/HBAN bank builds.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A card lender's owner earnings are net income less the equity it must retain to fund receivables growth at its CET1 target; everything above that is distributable (SYF pays out ~100% via buybacks). We capitalise that FCFE at a 12% cost of equity on a through-cycle 28% pretax margin, so a credit downturn is inside the base case, and model a full recession in the bear.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: every 1pp of net charge-offs on ~$100B receivables is ~$1.0B pretax (~23% of FY26E pretax)
Partner concentration and RSA renegotiation (Walmart/OnePay execution, Amazon, PayPal renewals)
CFPB/state late-fee and add-on product rulemaking
Deposit pricing and NIM as the Fed cuts
Capital rules (Basel III endgame, CCAR SCB) constraining the buyback pace
